# Warranties

US commercial-market reference points; verify against the matter's
jurisdiction pack — the enforceability and required form of warranty
disclaimers varies by jurisdiction.

## Balanced position

The provider warrants that the service or deliverables will materially
conform to the documentation or specifications, that services will be
performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, and that it will comply
with applicable law in performing. Each party warrants it has authority to
enter the agreement. Implied warranties are disclaimed conspicuously, but the
express warranties stand behind the core commitment. Warranty remedies are
repair/re-performance or replacement, backed by a refund right if the
provider cannot cure.

```example
Provider warrants that (a) the Service will materially conform to the
Documentation, and (b) professional services will be performed in a
professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards. As
Customer's exclusive remedy for breach of this warranty, Provider shall
re-perform the affected services or correct the non-conformity; if Provider
cannot do so within thirty (30) days, Customer may terminate the affected
order and receive a refund of prepaid fees for the unperformed portion.
```

## Common one-sided variants

**Tilted toward the provider:**
- "As is" disclaimer reaching the core commitment itself — the service is
  promised in the order form and unpromised in the warranty section.
- Sole remedy is re-performance at the provider's discretion with no refund
  backstop, making the warranty illusory.
- Warranty claim window so short (e.g., days from delivery) that defects
  cannot realistically be discovered in time.

**Tilted toward the customer:**
- Open-ended fitness-for-purpose warranties measured against the customer's
  subjective business outcomes.
- One-sided compliance-with-laws warranty covering laws applicable to the
  customer's industry rather than to the provider's performance.
- Warranties that operate as uncapped indemnities by feeding into a carve-out
  from the liability cap.

## Fallback ladder

1. Conformance + professional-performance warranties; conspicuous disclaimer
   of implied warranties; cure-then-refund remedy (preferred).
2. Accept exclusive warranty remedies if the refund/termination backstop is
   preserved when cure fails.
3. Accept a defined warranty period (commonly 90 days to 12 months for
   deliverables) running from delivery or acceptance, with notice required
   within the period rather than within days of discovery.
4. Accept "as is" only for genuinely as-is items (beta features, free tiers,
   third-party components), expressly carved out from the paid core service.

Below rung 4 — an "as is" core service or a discretionary-only remedy —
escalate.

**Rationale:** A warranty is only as real as its remedy; review the remedy
and the disclaimer's reach before the warranty's wording.
